evidence_scope_projection.definition: Overall prostate cancer evidence, excluding estimates solely about aggressive prostate cancer. General estimates from papers that also report aggressive endpoints remain included. Uncertain endpoints retain their existing review and pooling restrictions.

studies.Authors: Chavarro JE, Stampfer MJ, Li H, Campos H, Kurth T, Ma J
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.Population: Apparently healthy men who provided blood samples in 1982
studies.Reference: A prospective study of polyunsaturated fatty acid levels in blood and prostate cancer risk.
studies.Timing: Blood collected in 1982 with 13 years of follow-up
studies.direction_imputation_reason: Comparison direction was not explicit; the protocol assumes high versus low exposure.
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Blood fatty acid levels were determined

cases.excerpt: Blood fatty acid levels were determined for 476 men diagnosed with prostate cancer during a 13-year follow-up and their matched controls.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Blood levels of gamma-linolenic and dihomo-gamma-linolenic acids, fatty acids resulting from the metabolism of linoleic acid, were directly associated with prostate cancer (RR, 1.41; 95% CI, 0.94-2.12; P(trend) = 0.05 for gamma-linolenic and RR, 1.54; 95% CI, 1.03-2.30; P(trend) = 0.02 for dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid).

design.excerpt: A nested case-control study was conducted

effect_size.excerpt: Whole blood levels of all long-chain n-3 fatty acids examined and of linoleic acid were inversely related to overall prostate cancer risk (RR(Q5vs.Q1), 0.59; 95% CI, 0.38-0.93; P(trend) = 0.01 for total long-chain n-3 fatty acids and RR(Q5vs.Q1), 0.62; 95% CI, 0.41-0.95; P(trend) = 0.03 for linoleic). Blood levels of gamma-linolenic and dihomo-gamma-linolenic acids, fatty acids resulting from the metabolism of linoleic acid, were directly associated with prostate cancer (RR, 1.41; 95% CI, 0.94-2.12; P(trend) = 0.05 for gamma-linolenic and RR, 1.54; 95% CI, 1.03-2.30; P(trend) = 0.02 for dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid).
